newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Sidor output rises 14 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Sidor output rises 14 pct in 1996.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned steel company Sidor, due to be privatized early next year, raised its production by 14 percent to 3.194 million tonnes of liquid steel in 1996, according to official figures obtained by Reuters.
The 1996 production estimate, up from 2.791 million tonnes in 1995, was contained in a table of results for companies in state holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana.
According to the table, Sidor will sell 2.687 million tonnes of liquid steel this year, up 24 percent from 2.17 million tonnes in 1995.
The increase in output comes despite a small reduction in staff from 11,952 to 11,452, the table showed.

The improved output was not enough to prevent Sidor making an expected net loss of 29.605 billion bolivars ($63 million). This was, however, an improvement on last year's loss of 71.496 billion bolivars ($246 million at the exchange rate at the end of 1995).
Operating profits are expected to rise to 66.935 billion bolivars ($142 million) from 30.835 billion bolivars ($106 million) last year.
Eleven groups have qualified to participate in the sale of Sidor.
The eleven groups include five from Mexico, two from Brazil, one from Japan, one from South Korea, one from Argentina and one from Venezuela.
The Mexican companies which qualified were Hylsamex SA, Imexsa, Sicartsa, Grupo Acero del Norte and Ahmsa and Grupo Siderurgica Panamericana.
From Brazil Usiminas and Companhia Siderurgica Nacional have qualified.
Japan's Kobe Steel Ltd, South Korea's Dongkuk

Steel Group, Argentina's Siderar SAIC and Venezuela's Sivensa make up the rest of the qualified companies selected in consultation with U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers which is handling the Sidor sale.
